title: Invisible fasten off
subtitle: Closing the last round without a visible join
excerpt: The standard fasten off leaves a slight jog where the last stitch meets the first. The invisible fasten off mimics the top of a stitch using the yarn tail and a tapestry needle, closing the round cleanly. Useful on any round piece where the join would otherwise show.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book — fasten off techniques. Standard modern crochet finishing.

glossaryTerms.definition: A finishing technique where the yarn tail is threaded on a tapestry needle and woven under the top loops of the adjacent stitch to simulate a complete stitch top, hiding the end of the last round.
The visible step that occurs when the end of a round meets the beginning of the same round, because the last stitch and the first stitch are worked at slightly different heights.

heroPrompt: Close-up of the top round of a hat in cream DK cotton — the last round completed with an invisible fasten off, the join between the first and last stitch of the round completely hidden.

content.text: When you work the last round of a hat or flat motif and close with a normal slip-stitch join, the join creates a small
— the last stitch is slightly taller than the first because of the starting chain. The
corrects this by threading the tail through the loops of the neighbouring stitch to mimic a complete stitch top.
Complete the last stitch of the round. Do not join with a slip stitch. Cut the yarn, leaving a 20 cm tail, and pull the tail through the live loop to secure.
Thread the tail on a tapestry needle.
Insert the needle from front to back under BOTH loops of the first stitch of the round (the one that followed the starting chain). Pull through.
Insert the needle back down through the back loop only of the last stitch you made (the one the tail is coming out of). Pull through snugly.
The tail now forms a false stitch top that mirrors the other stitches in the round. Weave in the tail on the wrong side.
The last round of a hat brim where the join will be visible in wear.
The last border round of a flat motif where a visible join would break the pattern.
Any colour change in rounds where the colour join needs to be invisible.
On flat pieces worked in rows (scarves, blankets, garment panels), the standard fasten off is sufficient — there is no circular join to disguise.
